finding.statement: Liames LLC applied to rezone thirteen parcels of which five, carrying 10.45 of the 31.82 acres, stood in three other names in the county's parcel layer — a family partnership with three of them, an apartment company, and an owner-occupier.
finding.and_the_caveat: AS OF ~2025-07-25, WHICH IS ELEVEN MONTHS BEFORE THE APPLICATION WAS DOCKETED. Applicant's counsel told the trustees the parcels are "owned by Liames, LLC" and that the structures on them "have been razed." Two readings survive and NEITHER is adopted: (a) the five transferred after the CAMA snapshot, which is entirely ordinary and would make counsel's statement correct; (b) the application ran over land Liames did not hold of record, which R.C. 519.12 permits. This corpus previously carried the five as unnamed and the gap as "the CAMA layer's ~2025-07 vintage, not a research gap"; that reading survives, and the five are now named. The Wood County Recorder's chronological index closes it. [open]

rezoned_2026_07_07.name_collision_warning: P&J THAYER FAMILY LTD and P&J THAYER FAMILY LIMITED PARTNERSHIP are served as two distinct `Deeded_Name` strings for what is almost certainly one partnership; they are carried separately because the layer serves them separately. Separately, #1436 flagged a LIMES family (Dale Limes LLC, Limes Real Estate Holdings LLC) holding several hundred acres on Devils Hole Road — one letter from LIAMES. Add to that list the Middleton Township FISCAL OFFICER, whose name is Laurie L. Limes and who signs every set of minutes in this collection. Three same-sounding names in one township record; no relationship among them is asserted, and the reason to write this down is that a name-match search WILL conflate them.

The Oppidan colocation site, 4.83 mi from the campus, in the City of Bowling Green. A SEPARATE PROJECT — see the register's standing warning against conflating the two.

limitations: NO RECORDER INSTRUMENT WAS READ. Every row here is the auditor's transfer record, not a deed. Grantors, recorder instrument numbers, deed book/page and the full chronological chain are all [open]. That is a per-source negative, not an absence — see record-watch.yaml → WOOD-COUNTY-RECORDER.
THE CAMA KEEPS ONLY THE LAST CONVEYANCE PER PARCEL. Everything before it is gone from this source by construction. The two consolidations erased eleven tracts' prices.
THE LAYER'S VINTAGE IS ~2025-07-25 and has not advanced in a year. Nothing here is a statement about 2026.

LIAMES, LLC'S OWN REGISTRATION IS [open]. title: Wood County Commissioners Resolution 23-01249 — Authorize Community Reinvestment Area Agreement between Liames LLC and Wood County, Ohio, 2023-09-28
warnings: OCR source, no text layer. Resolution number and title are cross-checked against the printed listing; free prose is as OCRed.
Every dollar and job figure here is a statement MADE at the meeting, not a term of the executed agreement. The agreement, the CRA boundary and the three school compensation agreements are all [open].
"approximately 300-400 square feet" is carried verbatim and is not plausible on its face. Do not cite it as a building size.

fields.instrument: Wood County Commissioners Resolution 23-01249 — Authorize Community Reinvestment Area Agreement between Liames LLC and Wood County, Ohio, 2023-09-28
fields.body: Board of County Commissioners, Wood County, Ohio
fields.journalled_in: Resolution 23-01253 (2023-10-03), "In the matter of approval of prior meeting minutes from the regular session held on September 28, 2023."                        # [verified]
fields.title_verbatim: AUTHORIZE COMMUNITY REINVESTMENT AREA AGREEMENT BETWEEN LIAMES LLC AND WOOD COUNTY, OHIO

vote.motion: approve resolution 23-01249 (the CRA agreement with Liames LLC)
vote.tally_verbatim: All voted aye and the motion carried.
vote.note: The item was PULLED from the consent listing at the start of the day ("with the exception of resolutions 23-01249 (Community Reinvestment Area Agreement) and 23-01250 ... which will be held until later in the day's session") and taken up as a separate 10:15 a.m. session, concluding 10:28 a.m. — thirteen minutes. [verified]

beneficiary.name: Liames, LLC
beneficiary.described_as: "Liames LLC plans to construct one or more data center buildings on property located at State Route 582 and Mercer Road in Middleton Township."                # [verified] as said
beneficiary.note: THE END USE IS ON A PUBLIC RECORD ON 2023-09-28. That is nineteen months before the 2025-04-09 Meta announcement and three days after the first Liames deed was recorded. The NDA concealed the OPERATOR; it did not conceal that the land would become data centers, nor the location, nor the scale. Nothing in this journal names Meta.

school_compensation.statement_verbatim: "He noted that Eastwood and Otsego Local Schools, as well as Penta Career Center, have already approved agreements accepting the terms of a tax abatement for the company. The local school districts are estimated to receive approximately $1 million annually."
school_compensation.ISSUE_BODY_CORRECTION: ISSUE #1438 SAYS "~$900k-1M/yr EACH". The journal says "The local school districts are estimated to receive approximately $1 million annually" — one figure, for the districts plural. Whether that is per district or in aggregate is genuinely ambiguous on the face of the sentence, and it is left ambiguous here rather than resolved in either direction; the compensation agreements themselves are the instrument and they are [open]. Note also that the journal names THREE parties — the issue names two. Penta Career Center is a joint vocational school district and was omitted from the register until now.
school_compensation.sequencing_note: [verified] All three school bodies had ALREADY approved before the county acted. The township passed its own resolution of support eight days earlier (2023-09-20). The county resolution is the last signature on a chain, not the first.

representations.statement_verbatim: "The new data centers will create 50 full-time jobs resulting in an estimated $4,000,000 annual payroll."
representations.speaker: Wade Gottschalk, Wood County Economic Development executive director
representations.note: THIS IS HALF THE JOB COUNT NOW IN CIRCULATION. Meta's own 2026-01-07 letter to the Middleton Township trustees says "at least 100 operational jobs," and the register carries ~100 permanent at an average in the mid-$80,000s. The abatement was granted against a representation of 50. $4,000,000 / 50 = $80,000 average, which is consistent with the later per-job figure — so what changed is the headcount, not the wage. [inference] on the arithmetic; the reason for the change is [open], and note the two figures were made by different parties at a two-and-a-half-year interval, so this is not necessarily a revision of the same estimate.

representations.statement_verbatim: "Mr. Gottschalk stated the new facilities will be low impact for the area and will not create truck traffic."
representations.speaker: Wade Gottschalk

representations.statement_verbatim: "Commissioner Bowlus asked about the size of the buildings. Mr. Knezevic stated the buildings will be approximately 300-400 square feet."
representations.speaker: Chris Knezevic, Vorys (for the applicant)
representations.note: CARRIED VERBATIM AND FLAGGED, NOT CORRECTED. As printed this is three orders of magnitude below the 715,000 sq ft initial phase Meta later disclosed, and it is not plausible on its face — an omitted "thousand" in the minutes is the obvious reading, and 300,000-400,000 sq ft per building against a 715,000 sq ft two-building initial phase would reconcile almost exactly. It is left as the record has it because this corpus does not silently repair a public body's minutes, and because the transcription is OCR: the possibility that the printed page says something else is real and is why this is [reference] with the quote attached. [inference] on the reconciliation, [open] on what the page actually says.

representations.statement_verbatim: "Commissioner Bowlus asked if the number of employees could increase. Mr. Knezevic stated he is not certain but there is potential for further expansion."
representations.speaker: Chris Knezevic

tif.statement_verbatim: "Mr. Gottschalk mentioned that a Tax Increment Financing agreement is also to be considered at a later date that would follow the 15-year tax abatement."
tif.note: ISSUE #1438 LISTS "the follow-on TIF" AS AN INSTRUMENT TO PULL, WHICH PRESUPPOSES IT EXISTS. As of 2023-09-28 it was a future item, described as FOLLOWING the fifteen-year abatement — i.e. from roughly 2039. No Wood County TIF for this project was located. That negative is weak and is stated as such: the county's static minutes tree stops at 2024-05-30 and the CivicEngage Agenda Center that succeeded it does not index the commissioners' minutes full-text (a search for "tax increment" across all its categories returns nothing, and so does a search for "Meta"). See record-watch.yaml → WOOD-COUNTY-TIF. [open] NOT TO BE CONFUSED WITH THE ABBOTT TIF: the City of Bowling Green's own community action plan states "City Council passed an ordinance with a TIF agreement for Abbott Industries in November 2023" — a different party, a different body, a different project, one month apart.

public_comment.speaker: Ross Fought
public_comment.status: A township resident. He appears in the county journal's attendance recital alongside staff, which reads as if he were an official; the Middleton Township minutes of 2023-10-04 settle it — "Resident Ross Fought shared his concerns over the tax abatement that was provided to Liames, LLC". [verified]
public_comment.statement_summary: Lives west of the proposed site; not against economic development or this project in particular, but "concerned with the tax abatement" — that "giving away property tax revenue is concerning," that "property taxes are going up and Wood County property owners will be paying their share while a new company has their taxes abated for 15 years," that the county "has numerous assets available to bring businesses without having to offer tax abatements," and that "Wood County is doing well and there is no need to give away the county coffers."
public_comment.note: The only public comment recorded on this item, and it was opposed. He raised the same objection to the township six days later. Recorded because the completeness of a public record's comment section is itself evidence.

appearances.economic_development: Wade Gottschalk (Wood County Economic Development, executive director)

disclosures.statement_verbatim: "He noted that by utilizing the acreage in question the concerns about road access onto Mercer Road could have less impact."
disclosures.note: The stated rationale is a site-access problem on Mercer Road — six months before the first Liames deed (2023-09-05) and two and a half years before the applicant's counsel told the trustees, at the 2026-07-07 hearing, that "Mercer Road is not being utilized for this project." The record does not say who raised the access concern or on whose behalf, and no inference is drawn about coordination; what is [verified] is that a Mercer Road access constraint was already shaping this township's zoning map in March 2023.

linkage.note: WHETHER THIS 80 ACRES IS INSIDE THE LIAMES ASSEMBLAGE IS NOT ESTABLISHED. The minutes name no parcel, and the committed parcel layer records only the LAST conveyance per parcel, so a 2023 Getz-to-Liames transfer would have been overwritten by the 2025-04-09 consolidation quitclaims. What is [verified] independently: by 2024-03-20 the township's own zoning inspector described Liames LLC as "property owners of the recently rezoned parcels between St. Rt. 582, St. Rt. 25 and Mercer Road," and by 2023-09-20 the CRA application covered "the rezoned properties within the CRA boundaries." The Wood County Recorder is the instrument that would close it; see record-watch.yaml → WOOD-COUNTY-RECORDER.

The minutes recite Wood County Planning Commission approval on 2023-03-07 and Middleton Township Zoning Commission approval on 2023-04-12, both after the filename's year. An abstention on both Busch matters and participation on the Liames matter is a fact about the record; any interest that would explain it is [open] and would be established by an Ohio Ethics Commission disclosure or a deed, neither of which is in the corpus.

Huffman appears again at the 2024-11-20 rezonings as the Wood County Port Authority's representative FOR the private sellers, and in the county journal of 2023-09-28 as Northwestern Water & Sewer District legal counsel. title: Middleton Township Trustees — statement of support for the Liames LLC Community Reinvestment Area application to the Wood County Commissioners, 2023-09-20
warnings: Every figure here is a statement made by a promoter at a public meeting. The minutes verify that it was said. They do not verify the investment total, and no agreement in the corpus states it.

fields.instrument: Middleton Township Trustees — statement of support for the Liames LLC Community Reinvestment Area application to the Wood County Commissioners, 2023-09-20
fields.body: Board of Trustees, Middleton Township, Wood County, Ohio

vote.motion_verbatim: "to state their support of the Community Reinvestment Area Application as provided to the Wood County Commissioners for a 75% tax abatement for 15 years, with the school districts being awarded in full, as applied for by Liames LLC for a data center"

disclosures.statement_verbatim: "[The] Community Reinvestment Area (CRA) application that will be presented to the Wood County Commissioners on September 28. The application provides a 75% tax abatement for 15 years and was applied for by Liames LLC for a Data Center on the rezoned properties within the CRA boundaries. Mr. Gottschalk noted it is a $750M investment in the township for a data center by a Fortune 200 company."
disclosures.speaker: Wade Gottschalk, Wood County Economic Development executive director
disclosures.note: THREE THINGS ARE ESTABLISHED HERE THAT THE REGISTER PREVIOUSLY CARRIED AS PRESS. (1) The end use — "a Data Center" — is stated on a township agenda on 2023-09-20. (2) The $750M figure, which the register carries as a "[reference] pro-forma / DCD framing," is the county's own economic-development director speaking at a public meeting; that it was SAID is [verified], the figure itself remains a projection and stays [reference], but its provenance is now a public body's minutes rather than trade press. (3) The properties were ALREADY REZONED by 2023-09-20 — "on the rezoned properties within the CRA boundaries" — which is the township's own confirmation that the seller-name rezonings of March and May 2023 preceded the assembly's public phase. Note also "Fortune 200 company": the county knew the counterparty's scale and did not name it. Meta was Fortune 200 in 2023; so were roughly two hundred others, and no identification is made from this line.

disclosures.statement_verbatim: "Eastwood School Board met with regard to the funding to the schools and approved their support. Otsego School Board meets soon to review the data as well as Penta Vocational Center."
disclosures.note: Establishes the order: Eastwood first, Otsego and Penta still to come, all three before the county's 2023-09-28 vote. "Penta Vocational Center" here and "Penta Career Center" in the county journal are the same body under two renderings; both are carried.

disclosures.statement: The township's motion conditions its support on "the school districts being awarded in full" — a schools-made-whole framing in the township's own words. What "in full" means in the executed compensation agreements is [open].

aggregate.statement: 91 + 68 + 75 + 37 = 271 acres of A-1 land brought toward M-1 by four separate landowners around this campus between August 2024 and September 2025, of which 91 were rezoned and 180 were withdrawn before a vote. Arithmetic on [verified] figures; the figures are the minutes' own approximations ("approximately"), so the total is approximate too.
aggregate.do_not_read_as: NOT a Meta land assembly. None of these four applicants is Liames, none of the named parcels is in the committed assemblage, and the only one with a stated buyer position said there was none. What the pattern establishes is a market forming around a disclosed campus, which is a different and weaker claim than assembly — and it is the weaker claim this corpus makes.

fields.instrument: Middleton Township Trustees — action on Application 2026041 (Liames, LLC), rezoning thirteen parcels in Section 19 to M-1 Light Industrial, 2026-07-07
fields.body: Board of Trustees, Middleton Township, Wood County, Ohio
fields.legal_notice: Published in the Sentinel-Tribune, 2026-06-20, and read into the record by the Fiscal Officer.                                                                 # [verified]
fields.outcome_note: [verified] — the minutes state it in terms: "It is noted the application was approved for rezoning. The application will be filed with the Wood County Recorder and also sent to the Wood County Planning Commission."

vote.motion: "to approve the recommendation of the Middleton Township Zoning Commission for the purpose of rezoning thirteen (13) parcels to M-1 based on the details noted in the application"
vote.effect: [verified] The motion was to ADOPT the zoning commission's recommendation, and that recommendation was to DENY. It failed 1-2, and the minutes record the rezoning as approved.
vote.press_discrepancy: SECONDARY REPORTING HAS THIS BACKWARDS AND SO DID THIS REPO. The register carried "trustees granted it anyway, 2-1 ... Mike Moulton and Fred Vetter in favor, Melissa Petrea against" [reference]. On the face of the minutes the vote is 1-2, and the single YES is PETREA — the trustee reported as the dissenter. Both accounts agree on the outcome and on who was on which side of it; they disagree on the direction of the question. A reader given only the press number would state the tally, the majority and the dissenter's name wrongly while stating the result rightly. The minutes are the record. WHY THIS READING AND NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE. The motion text can be read a second way — "approve the recommendation ... for the purpose of rezoning" as simply "approve the rezoning" — but that reading does not survive its own roll call: 1-2 would then have DEFEATED the rezoning, and the next sentence of the same minutes says it was approved. Only the reading above is self-consistent with the outcome the minutes state. What is NOT resolved is WHY the question was put that way: a deliberate procedural device, an error at the meeting, or a clerical error in the minutes are all live, the minutes give no reason, and none is asserted. The Wood County Recorder's copy of the filed rezoning would corroborate the outcome but not the framing. [open]

parcels.printed_as: The minutes print the auditor's full dashed form (J34-/J36- district prefix + 3-digit map + 12 digits). The committed parcel layer stores the 15-digit remainder — see the deed_id_regex caveat on WOOD_PARCEL_SCHEMA — so both forms are carried.
parcels.stated_purpose: "construction logistics" — the applicant's own words, as recited by the Wood County Planning Commission's 2026-06-02 agenda; at the hearing counsel framed it as creating "a contiguous M1 zoning for the parcels owned by Liames, LLC".      # [verified]
parcels.acreage_reconciliation: [verified] The thirteen deeded acreages sum to 31.820 — the Wood County Planning Commission's "approximately 31.82 acres" to the hundredth. The 31.82 figure had been carried as press [reference]; it is now a measurement against the auditor's own layer. The eight Liames-name parcels carry 21.37 ac and the other five 10.45 ac.
parcels.ownership_caveat: FIVE OF THE THIRTEEN DO NOT STAND IN LIAMES' NAME IN THE COUNTY'S PARCEL LAYER, AND THAT IS A STATEMENT ABOUT JULY 2025, NOT ABOUT THE HEARING. The `cama_deeded_name` above is from a live query of Wood County's Vision_Parcels layer on 2026-08-05, which returned the same 73,839 rows and the same maximum Sale_Date of 2025-07-25 that #1436 recorded — zero rows transfer after that date, so the layer has not been refreshed in more than a year and any transfer after 2025-07-25 is invisible to it. Applicant's counsel told the trustees the parcels are "owned by Liames, LLC" and that "structures on the properties have been razed." title: Bowling Green Water Pollution Control (WPC)
warnings: Table 12's low flows are NOT measured on Poe Ditch, and not measured anywhere near Bowling Green. They are drainage-area-adjusted from USGS gauge 04195500 (Portage River at Woodville) over 1951-97 — a record that closed before the network's own derived 7Q10 window (1980-2024) opens. The footnote is explicit: "Flow data from Low-Flow Characteristics of Stream in Ohio through Water Year 1997 and adjusted for drainage area." Treat the 0.364 cfs as the REGULATORY denominator that this permit's limits were actually computed against, not as a measurement of the ditch, and do not reconcile it against a derived value by preferring one — they are different arithmetic over different records. Same posture as Ottawa (data/extracted/oepa/ottawa/2PD00028.fs.npdes.yaml).

The plant is far larger than the water it discharges into. Table 12 states the discharger flow as 15.47 cfs (10 MGD) against an annual 7Q10 of 0.364 cfs in the same table — a ratio of about 42 to 1. Under design-flow low-flow conditions Poe Ditch below this outfall is effluent, not diluted effluent. This is a [verified] reading of two numbers printed in one table; the ratio itself is arithmetic and is tagged [inference] where it is asserted downstream.

The water quality criteria applied to this discharge are NOT Poe Ditch's own. Poe Ditch is designated Limited Resource Water; the fact sheet states on p. 6 that the criteria associated with the North Branch Portage River's higher uses (Warmwater Habitat, Primary Contact Recreation) "are applied to Bowling Green WPC to be protective of this higher quality stream." A screen that reads Poe Ditch's LRW designation and stops there will apply the wrong criteria.

The total phosphorus limit was NOT tightened by this permit. The reduction from 1.0 to 0.7 mg/L happened in the PRIOR action, permit 2PD00009*SD (p. 9: "the monthly average limit for total phosphorus was reduced from 1.0 to 0.7 mg/L in permit 2PD00009*SD"). This *TD renewal CONTINUES it — "this permit proposes that the same phosphorus limits be continued under the adaptive management approach." Any claim that the 2022 renewal cut the phosphorus limit is wrong; the 2022 renewal declined to cut it further while Ohio EPA waited to resurvey.

The TMDL's own target for this plant is 0.5 mg/L total phosphorus and it was never adopted as a limit. Page 9: the TMDL "assessed multiple scenarios for assigning phosphorus reductions but none resulted in reaching the in-stream target," and it "recommended an implementation strategy ... with a target effluent concentration of 0.5 mg/L for Bowling Green WPC but no formal wasteload allocation was approved." The operative 0.7 mg/L limit rests on best technical judgement, not on an approved WLA.

warnings: THE LIMIT TABLE YOU WANT DEPENDS ON THE DATE. Part I.A carries TWO complete limit tables for the same outfall. Item 1 governs "the period beginning on the effective date of this permit and lasting through the 36th month"; Item 2 governs "the period beginning on 37th month after the effective date of this permit and lasting until the expiration date." The interim table has NO MBAS limit and NO B2EHP limit, and its ammonia limits are looser (winter 7.3/4.8 mg/L, summer 2.7/1.8 mg/L). Ambient stations 801 and 901 monitor the NORTH BRANCH PORTAGE RIVER, not Poe Ditch. The permit's own upstream/downstream biology and chemistry are therefore measured a stream removed from the outfall's immediate receptor. Poe Ditch itself is not monitored under this permit at all.

new_or_tightened.note_other: B2EHP and the lower summer/winter ammonia limits also first apply here. The full final set matches Table 15 of the fact sheet; see data/extracted/oepa/bowling-green/2PD00009.fs.npdes.yaml rather than duplicating it.

schedule_of_compliance.subject: Final Effluent Limits for Ammonia, B2EHP, and MBAS
schedule_of_compliance.preamble: "New final effluent limits are proposed for bis(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (B2EHP), and methyl blue activated substances (MBAS). Also, lower final effluent limits are proposed for ammonia (summer and winter). The permittee shall attain compliance with the effluent limits for ammonia, B2EHP, and MBAS as expeditiously as possible but no later than the dates in the following schedule."

milestones.requirement: Progress report to Ohio EPA Northwest District Office (NWDO) including five years of influent/effluent/sludge data for ammonia, B2EHP and MBAS; a list of significant and non-significant industrial users; actions taken in the previous 12 months; actions planned for the next 12.

"As soon as possible but no later than 36 months after the effective date of this permit, the permittee shall attain compliance with the new effluent limits for ammonia, B2EHP, and MBAS. The permittee shall notify Ohio EPA NWDO within seven days of attaining compliance."

schedule_of_compliance.due_date_note: The calendar dates in `due` are [inference] — computed from the 2022-05-01 effective date; the permit states only the month offsets. Whether the two progress reports and the compliance notification were actually submitted is NOT established by any captured source. [open] — a records request to Ohio EPA NWDO for the 07099 and 05699 submittals would settle it, and would speak directly to what the plant knew about its MBAS position before the limit took effect.

other_schedules.phosphorus_optimization: Part I.C.B — the permittee must complete and submit the "Evaluation for Reducing Discharge of Phosphorus" form with its next NPDES renewal application.
other_schedules.municipal_pretreatment: Part I.C.C — evaluate the adequacy of local industrial user limitations, submit a revised local limit technical justification report, and implement revisions if needed. Relevant to any new significant industrial user in the service area.

other_requirements_of_note.percent_removal: Item M — "The treatment works must obtain at least 85 percent removal of carbonaceous [BOD5 and TSS]."
other_requirements_of_note.reopener: Item N — "Water quality based permit limitations in this permit may be revised based on updated [information]." A reopener exists; nothing in the captured record shows it used.
other_requirements_of_note.weekend_monitoring: Item C — all parameters except flow "need not be monitored on days when the plant is not normally staffed (Saturdays, Sundays, and Holidays)." Report "AN" on those days. Worth carrying: a daily-maximum limit is only sampled on staffed days, so the reported daily maxima are not a seven-day-per-week record.
other_requirements_of_note.ssos: Item H — SSO reporting, including a separate track for SSOs that imminently and substantially endanger human health.
